1.why: Verify-token only accepts the token hash on the recovery bound to the current session via sessionId and currentRecovery().

2.why: Each recovery has its own random tokenHash tied to one session; another session’s recovery cannot validate that token.

3.why: Completing verify-mfa never deletes or rotates other sessions; only the recovery record is marked completed.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS and non-HTTPS URLs are rejected, but no minimum TLS version is explicitly pinned.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as argon2id; contact is not retained, though ‘encrypted’ is imprecise.

6.why: No real email is sent; API messages are generic and never include the submitted contact or other private fields.

7.why: Inputs are validated (validContact, validToken, validMfaCode, strongPassword) and the UI only uses textContent, not raw HTML.

8.why: No redirect parameter is accepted; client routing is hash-only to fixed stages on the same origin.

9.why: There are no email templates that embed user input; contact is never reflected into HTML or messages.

10.why: testToken and testMfaCode are returned in API JSON and written into the on-page delivery log panel.

11.why: Passwords use argon2id in memory, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded string 482913 in source.

12.why: No login accounts or default credentials exist in the application.

13.why: recoveryLimit, tokenLimit, passwordLimit, and mfaLimit lock out further attempts after thresholds within LIMIT_WINDOW/LOCK_WINDOW.

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same generic ‘If recovery is available…’ message whether or not contact is valid.

15.why: Reset tokens are crypto randomHex(32) values, 64 hex chars, hashed and bound to that session’s recovery only.
